evals.prompt: Our strategic plan at Coastal Youth Sailing Foundation (San Diego, $2.2M, 18 staff, 13-member board) expires June 2027. Last time a consultant wrote a 40-page plan with 9 priorities that nobody looked at again. The board wants a new plan adopted by May. Design the process for us.
evals.expected_output: A five-phase process (scope, scan, focus, draft, adopt) with a planning committee, time-boxed scan including beneficiary/funder input and trend data, a priority-setting retreat narrowing to 3–5 priorities with a stop-doing list, a short plan plus plan-on-a-page, and adoption with an owner and quarterly check-ins.
assertions: Structures the process in phases from scoping through board adoption with a 4–6 month timeline that fits the May deadline
Sets up a planning committee (board chair, ED, a few board members and senior staff) with the full board approving
Includes a time-boxed environmental scan with separate staff and board SWOT sessions, PEST, financial/program trend data, and input from participants/families, funders and partners
Plans a priority-setting retreat with the scan summary circulated in advance, narrowing to 3–5 priorities and naming what the org will stop doing
Requires each annual objective to have an owner and metric and produces a short plan plus a one-page plan-on-a-page
Addresses the last plan's shelving by naming an internal plan owner, a quarterly board check-in and annual refresh

evals.prompt: quick sanity check on our draft priorities: 1) run excellent programs 2) grow revenue 3) expand to Oceanside 4) improve staff culture 5) upgrade tech 6) build brand 7) strengthen board 8) DEI. board retreat is saturday
evals.expected_output: Flags priority sprawl and operational duties restated as priorities, applies the stop-doing and tradeoff tests, and suggests consolidating to 3–5 real choices with goals, owners and metrics.
assertions: Flags 8 priorities as too many and recommends narrowing to 3–5
Identifies 'run excellent programs' (and similar baseline duties) as operational duties rather than strategic choices
Applies a test like 'what would we stop doing to fund this?' and recommends a stop-doing list
Suggests consolidating or demoting items into goals/objectives and notes each objective needs an owner and metric
Offers a retreat exercise (e.g., affinity clustering and dot-voting) for Saturday

evals.prompt: We're mid-crisis — our ED resigned last month, we lost a $400K county contract, and the board wants to do a full 5-year strategic plan right now so funders see we have direction. Our interim ED starts next week. Also someone suggested we use the plan to decide whether to start a fee-based program.
evals.expected_output: Recommends a 1-year bridge plan over a 5-year plan given crisis and transition, compresses the timeline appropriately, and routes the fee-based program feasibility to revenue diversification while naming it as a priority question.
assertions: Recommends a 1-year bridge plan rather than a 3- or 5-year plan for an organization in crisis or leadership transition
Notes the bridge plan can be compressed to a shorter timeline (roughly 6–8 weeks)
Routes evaluating the specific fee-based program to the revenue diversification skill while the plan names the priority and its measure
Flags resource implications (lost contract) to hand to budgeting before adoption
Insists the plan draw on financial and program trend data (e.g., the impact of the lost contract) rather than going straight to brainstorming

should_not_trigger.query: Build a logic model for our youth sailing program showing how lessons lead to confidence and STEM interest.
Help me set up quarterly Rocks and weekly L10 meetings to execute our new strategic plan.
